status: A record of how the code behaves, not a specification of intent. It began at 3ae1cdf as a snapshot with no fixes in it. Since then fixes are recorded here too, with their vectors: an entry marked fixed says what changed and how it behaves now, and an entry marked current behavior is still a snapshot.

AMOUNT_MAX.imd-flop: src/amount.ts AMOUNT_MAX (its own literal; test/contract.test.ts checks it against this value). knownAmount refuses an amount above it: unknown, never a guess. A day or job total above it is not a known amount either: run refuses (exit 3) and the read commands exit 1 (ledger.ts exactTotal)
AMOUNT_MAX.viewer: build-lane.py AMOUNT_MAX (read from this file): amount() refuses an amount above it
AMOUNT_MAX.note: 1e9 FLOP (swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 5; was 2^53 - 1). Up to 1e9 FLOP an amount x is on the 6 decimal grid when n = floor(x * 1e6 + 0.5) gives back the same double (n / 1e6 === x), and then n is its exact count of millionths. Totals are exact sums of those integers and the cap check is made in them, with no tolerance (review of the audit 33f3b9f fixes, defect 1). A total of exactly AMOUNT_MAX is a known amount; one millionth above is not. Above about 2^33 FLOP a double cannot hold the grid at all. spend-guard has no such bound. Proved by the property tests in imd-flop/test/audit-33f3b9f.test.ts, imd-flop/test/review-audit2.test.ts and the viewer twins

FLOP_DECIMALS.imd-flop: src/chain/describe.ts FLOP_DECIMALS (its own literal; test/chain-words.test.ts checks it against this value). The chain encoder writes every amount in raw units and in FLOP with it
FLOP_DECIMALS.note: money stage 1. Base units per FLOP are 10^18. Per FLOP's own sources, read 2026-11-11: the chain counts money in whole base units, 10^18 per FLOP, and its spec forbids floating point conversion in encoders. The viewer shows an exact amount as FLOP with this many decimals.

EXACT_AMOUNT_BOUND.note: money stage 1. 2^128, written as a digit string because a JSON number cannot hold it exactly. An exact amount is below it: per FLOP's own sources, read 2026-11-11, the chain holds money in a u128. The exact amount rule (amount.ts exactAmount, build-lane.py exact) is pinned by vectors/exact-amount.json.

SEAT_ID.note: swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 4: one spelling per seat. A seat id is the unassigned placeholder, or decimal digits with no leading zero (0 alone is allowed) of at most 63 digits. The chain reads a tokenId as a number, so 42 and 042 are one seat there. Before, both spellings were accepted and compared as text, so one seat could hold two keys, two caps and two daily totals. The 63 digit limit (review of the audit 33f3b9f fixes, defect 9; it replaces at most 2^256 - 1): a number of 64 digits or more cannot be told from a key by the secret scan, so no file of such a seat could be written. value.bytes: the file is bytes, decoded as UTF-8 the way Node does it: an invalid byte becomes U+FFFD and never aborts the file
value.line_end: lines end at \n (0x0A) only; a \r is an ordinary character, and JSON whitespace between tokens
value.numbering: lines are numbered from 1, blank ones included; a final empty piece after the last \n is not a line
value.blank_note: a line is blank when every character is one of these code points: exactly the characters JavaScript's String.prototype.trim removes, which is what imd-flop did before this contract
value.line: a line that is not blank and not nested too deep (see depth) is one JSON value in JSON.parse's grammar (NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are not JSON) and must be an object; anything else is unreadable, "not valid JSON" or "not a JSON object"
value.depth: a line nested deeper than max_depth levels is unreadable, "nested too deep", whether or not it is otherwise valid JSON. Depth is counted on the line's text before parsing: { and [ outside a JSON string open a level, } and ] close one, and a string runs from an unescaped " to the next unescaped " (a backslash in a string escapes the character after it). The row object itself is level 1
value.numbers: every number is read as a double; in the viewer an integer is parsed as float(text) and kept as an int only when that double is integral and at most 2^53 - 1, so a 4300 digit integer is Infinity in both parts and never meets Python's digit limit
value.booleans: a boolean is never a number
value.grouping: rows are grouped by REQUEST_ID; a row without a usable request id is a group of its own, keyed by its line
value.receipts: a receipt file is the whole file decoded the same way, one JSON value in JSON.parse's grammar that must be an object; anything else is unreadable; the depth rule applies to it too, counted on the whole file (review of the audit 33f3b9f fixes, defect 8; pinned by contract/fixtures/receipt-text/)

CAP_PROMISE.value: The promise is that the daily cap and the job budget are never passed without PAST_ADMITTED. It holds for a ledger that only this tool writes, and for a gateway that enforces the child key's cap. A ledger that was edited, moved, removed or damaged is outside the promise: the tool fails closed where it can see the damage, names the line, and prints PAST_ADMITTED where it can see a charge rise, and that is all it claims. Crashes of this tool itself, a torn line or a dead lock holder, are inside the promise. The ledger lock trusts that two processes that report the same host name share one process table. A home shared by machines or containers that report the same host name and have separate process tables is outside the promise. Within one process the lock is taken on its main thread only: a take from a worker thread is refused.
CAP_PROMISE.imd-flop: README.md, at the top of the spend rules (review fixes 4, item 9)

imd-flop counted only holder paid rows against the seat's daily cap (spentToday). With payer requester the daily cap did not apply: the only limits were the per-call cap and the job budget the caller supplies per job id, while the FLOP still came out of the seat's own gateway key. The viewer checked every row against the daily cap using spent_before, which on a requester row was the job's spend, and never showed the job budget (finding 5). spend-guard has no payer.
quirks.fixed_behavior: The seat's daily cap bounds every call the seat's key pays for, whoever the call is for. Today the gateway has no third party payment, so the seat's key pays for every call, and every call counts. Requester is an attribution label plus a second, narrower limit, the job budget. Limits by payer, in checked order: holder: daily cap. requester: daily cap, then job budget. imd-flop: spentToday sums every row of the seat for that provider and UTC day, with no payer filter. noRoom refuses on the first limit with nothing left. checkBudget, after noRoom and the per-call cap, refuses on the first limit the padded quote does not fit. Ledger rows: spent_before is the seat's spend today before the call, for every payer. job_spent_before is the job's requester spend before the call, and null on a holder row. viewer: SPEND_LIMITS lists the same limits in the same order, each with its own running total field. Review of the audit 8ddc5d2 fixes: the daily cap applies to every row, whatever its payer. A row whose payer is neither holder nor requester is checked against the daily cap, its spent_before read as the seat's total, and carries the spend flag 'payer unknown'. A requester row with no job_spent_before key was written before this rule, when its spent_before was the job's spend: its job budget left is job_budget - spent_before - cap_charge, and its daily cap cannot be checked. A limit that applies to a row and cannot be worked out (an input is unknown, or that case) shows a blank figure and '<limit> not checked'. That wording is a spend flag, or one amber chip in the place of the green chain final chip, which such a row never gets. The row keeps 'matches'. spend-guard has no payer and keeps no running total: it checks one call against one cap, so nothing changed there. Not built: when FLOP ships proxies or escrow pools and a call is funded by another account, that account's limit will bound the call and it will not count against the seat's cap. Pinned by cap-payer.json (imd-flop) and, in viewer-labels.json (viewer), the label-requester vectors, the label-unknown-payer vectors and label-holder-unknown-spent-before-daily-cap-not-checked.

quirks.summary: Within the scope of CAP_PROMISE (a ledger only this tool writes, a gateway that enforces the child key's cap), the daily cap (and a job budget) can be passed only by a booking above what the cap admitted for the request: its known booked charge, or its padded quote when that charge is not a known amount (review fixes 3 and 4). That is when the gateway shows a receipt for a request this tool recorded as never sent, when it reports more than the child key allowed, when a read raises a row an older version booked below its hold back toward it, when a damaged charge is repaired above the hold, or when the booking step writes run's sent row again after the ledger lost it. Every later row of such a request keeps PAST_ADMITTED in its reason. "Nothing was sent" is a local fact and releases the hold; a later trusted read that shows the gateway holds the request brings the hold back (the safe direction), and another call may have used the freed room meanwhile. A settled amount or a reported cost above the padded quote raises the charge above what the call was allowed to spend. None is silent: the booking prints PAST_ADMITTED on stderr and records it in the row's reason, and status marks today when today's total is above its cap (over_cap_today_utc in --json, OVER CAP in text). status marks today only: a hold that comes back on an earlier day is shown by its row's PAST_ADMITTED reason and by the viewer, which flags that row (review fixes 3). It stays as it is: refusing the read or keeping the hold released would understate what was spent. Pinned by vectors run-settled-above-hold-prints-past-admitted, run-reported-cost-above-hold-prints-past-admitted, refresh-presend-then-pending-hold-comes-back and refresh-presend-then-no-state-hold-comes-back.

Amounts are counted in whole millionths of a FLOP with no tolerance (review of the audit 33f3b9f fixes, defect 1; imd-flop rounding.ts gridMicro, ceilMicro and floorMicro, viewer build-lane.py grid_micro, ceil_micro and floor_micro, the same expressions). An amount x is on the grid when n = floor(x * 1e6 + 0.5) gives back the same double; then its count is n. Every amount the tools compare is at most AMOUNT_MAX, 1e9 FLOP, and up to there every grid amount is found this way. A day or job total is the exact sum of its charges' counts (imd-flop ledger.ts exactTotal). The cap check is made in the same integers in both parts: over when the charge is above the cap less the spend. So for amounts on the grid every total and every cap decision is exact, and the two parts agree on every one (contract/fixtures/cap-triples). Only an amount off the grid is rounded, checked by comparison: a charge or a spend up to the smallest step at or above it, a cap or a budget down to the largest step at or below it. So rounding never admits a call over the cap. What remains: an amount off the grid (a hand edit, a damaged row, or a gateway amount a booking raised the charge to, which prints PAST_ADMITTED) is counted at the next step, up to 1e-6 FLOP more than it is. It closes when money moves to exact base units (money stage 2). Pinned by contract/vectors/rounding.json, the cap.daily_left vectors in cap-compare.json, imd-flop/test/review-fixes.test.ts (R-g) and imd-flop/test/review-audit2.test.ts (review defect 1).

rules.text: Precedence: unreadable, then unknown, then identity mismatch, then disagree.
A failed read never shows 'matches' and never releases the reservation.
An unknown row beside a settled ledger keeps the reservation line and keeps chain-final green blocked.
The link column stays grey 'not checked' and never turns green from ledger data alone.

viewer_label_rules.referenced_by: Vectors name these ids in label_rules. Every id must be referenced by at least one vector; both loaders reject an unknown id.

vector_status.default: A vector without a status pins current behavior: each part asserts `expect`.
vector_status.known_defect: A vector with status "known_defect" names a defect id from known_defects. `expect` is today's exact output and IS asserted, so the suite stays green and documents the defect. `target` holds the agreed label per affected part and is NOT asserted yet; the step that fixes the defect moves `target` into `expect` and drops the status.
vector_status.fixed: A vector with status "fixed" names the defect (known_defects id) that a step 3 [fix: ...] commit closed. That commit moved the old target into expect, which IS asserted, and dropped target. A c7 snapshot case lists closed defects in fixed.

known_defects.fixed_behavior: settlement.ts decideBooking(prev, read, costReported) is the one decision: only a trusted read changes state or spend; a reported cost may raise a charge and never lowers it, on a hold and on a settlement alike; a read below a booked known settlement disagrees and state and spend stay; otherwise a proven settlement replaces the spend and its charge replaces the hold; the state never moves from settled/released to a pending state; a charge that is not a known amount is never replaced by a guess. booking.ts bookRead(h, requestId, read, info) is the one booking step: under the ledger lock it reads the latest row of the request, decides, and appends one row when a recorded field changes. run and receipt --refresh both call it. run prints DISAGREE on stderr when its own read is refused, as refresh does, and still records its reported cost and the HTTP status of its read. If the lock cannot be taken or the append fails after the paid call, run exits 1 as before: the sent row stays the latest row and keeps the reservation, and the answer is in the response file. Review of the booking step: the reported cost survives that. bookRead resolves the reported cost in one place: the caller's (only run has one), else the one the row records, else usage.cost_flop in the stored response file (response-store.ts storedReportedCost), each through reportedCost. A missing, unreadable or costless response file gives no cost, never 0. A later refresh so charges at least the reported cost and records it in cost_reported. Two trusted reads book the same spend and charge in either order. Pinned by imd-flop/test/booking.test.ts (the interleavings) and imd-flop/test/decision-properties.test.ts (the properties). The first build covered receipt reads only; the rows run writes when the paid call itself fails followed in KD-8. known_defects.source: independent review of the review fixes, finding R9 (high), 2026-11-11; rule decided by the owner (the hold floor)
known_defects.where: src/settlement.ts decideBooking: a proven settlement replaced the hold in the cap charge
known_defects.today: a settled or released read below the padded quote freed room the next call was admitted against; a later higher read of the first request, or the cost its completion reported, was then booked, and the day ended over the cap with no refusal. Reproduced: cap 0.3, A settles at 0.01, B is admitted at 0.186, a refresh of A reads settled 0.186, the day is 0.372
known_defects.target: from the moment a call is sent, its cap charge is never below the padded quote it was admitted with; a gateway read and a reported cost can only raise it
known_defects.decision: The hold floor. The cap charge counts what each call was allowed to spend, not what it ended up costing: max(padded quote, settled spend, reported cost). The spend field still records what the gateway says was spent. Reason: a gateway read is not final by the gateway's own schema (OpenAPI CredentialReceipt, read 2026-11-11: later reconciliation can change what a receipt shows), and the child key's cap, the padded quote, is the one bound the gateway enforces. The floor lifts only when the call's settlement is proven on chain; that proof does not exist yet, and decideBooking marks the one place where it will plug in. The one release that stays is "nothing was sent" (KD-13). Rows an older version booked below their hold are not migrated: a later read raises them back toward the hold and prints PAST_ADMITTED, since later calls were admitted against the lower charge.
known_defects.fixed_behavior: settlement.ts decideBooking books the charge from holdFloor: the booked charge; on a released row a trusted read reopens, the padded quote again (or the booked charge if higher); on a row whose charge is not a known amount, the padded quote for a read that proves a settlement, and nothing (the read disagrees) otherwise or when the padded quote is not a known amount. A settled amount and a reported cost raise it; nothing a gateway read says lowers it. Decision.pastAdmitted is set when the booking is above what the cap admitted for the request: its known booked charge, or its padded quote when that charge is not a known amount (residual R-f; review fixes 3 and 4: before, it compared with the padded quote only, so a row an older version booked below its hold climbed back silently, and in pass 3 a repair of an unknown charge above the hold said nothing). The booking step also marks a seed row written again, and carries the mark on every later row of the request. status shows today_utc (charged to the cap) beside gateway_spent_today_utc (what the gateway reported as spent) and over_cap_today_utc. The viewer agrees: build-lane.py below_hold flags a row the call was sent for (any state but refused_local) whose cap charge is a known amount below its known padded quote with the spend flag 'charged below its hold', marks it bad, and never gives it the green chip; rows an older version booked are not migrated, so the lane says so (viewer-labels.json, rule viewer.below_hold). Pinned by imd-flop/test/review-fixes.test.ts (R9), the hold floor block of imd-flop/test/decision-properties.test.ts, and the settlement vectors that book a settlement or a release.

known_defects.source: swarm audit of 33f3b9f (IMD job b4e8e103), finding 1 (high), with findings 7 and 11 item 1, 2026-11-11
known_defects.where: src/ledger.ts reclaimIfDead: a waiter read the owner of an old lock, then renamed whatever was at the lock path aside
known_defects.today: the reclaim of a dead holder's lock was not exclusive. Between a waiter's read of the owner and its rename, another waiter could reclaim the lock and a third take it; the rename then moved a live holder's lock aside, so two holders ran at once and the cap could be passed with no PAST_ADMITTED. Seen at c79dd6d with a pause of up to 40 ms after the owner read: two holders in 2 of 30 rounds
known_defects.target: nothing renames or moves the lock. A waiter removes it only when its recorded owner is provably dead (the same host and a pid that is gone, or this process's own pid with a token it does not hold now) and the waiter holds the reclaim right for that exact token, after it has read the lock again under the right. Age plays no part. A lock with no readable owner, a lock of another host and a lock whose owner is alive are never removed
known_defects.fixed_behavior: src/lock.ts holds the lock as steps that yield before every file operation. The reclaim right is the file <lock>.reclaim.<token>.<n>, created exclusively; it passes to the next level only when its owner is provably dead. Under the right the waiter reads the lock again and unlinks it only if it still carries that token, then removes its own right file. Every ledger append checks first that the lock still carries this process's token (ledger lock lost is a failed append). A token is 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, _ and -, so nothing read from a lock file becomes a path. Pinned by imd-flop/test/lock-model.test.ts (every interleaving of three waiters with crashes over an in memory file system; it fails for the old rule and for seven other wrong rules), test/lock.test.ts (the real file system, real processes killed at random moments) and test/review-lock.test.ts (the six defects of the independent review). Known and kept: one home under two spellings in one process is not re-entrant (the second take times out); a holder that has exited but is not yet reaped counts as alive; a process killed between creating its temporary file and writing it leaves an empty .tmp file that no rule removes; the lock is tested on Linux only.

Nothing is stored with null in place of a number the gateway sent
known_defects.fixed_behavior: src/providers.ts gives @flop-labs/client its own fetch for the paid call and the receipt read (src/outside-json.ts nonFiniteSeam, the client's documented fetch option). It calls the real fetch first, reads the body text once from a clone and runs the same number check as readOutsideJson. A body with a number that is not finite is handed to the client as a new Response with the same status and headers and the body non_finite_number, which is not JSON, so the client and everything above it take the path of a body that is not JSON. Any other body, and one whose read fails, is handed on unchanged. The seam never throws because of a body. Its note is a closure of one call; the provider reads it right after the call and notes the client's error by identity (markNonFinite; the error itself is not changed), so run.ts writes the reason in brackets: a 200 answer is timeout_unknown with the reservation held, reason FlopValidationError: no answer; spend unknown, not retried (non_finite_number), exit 6; an HTTP error answer is HTTP <status> (non_finite_number). A receipt read is http 0 with error Gateway response is not valid JSON (non_finite_number), or the HTTP status with error non_finite_number, so a 401 sets no key_expired flag; it books nothing.
